name: Mumbai University (MU)
desc: Calculate your Mumbai University (MU) CGPA to percentage using the official formula: Percentage = (7.1 × CGPA) + 11.
faq1: The formula used by Mumbai University is: Percentage = (7.1 × CGPA) + 11
faq2: A CGPA of 7.0 is equivalent to 60.7% in Mumbai University.

name: VTU (Karnataka)
desc: Convert VTU CGPA to percentage instantly using the official VTU grading formula.
faq1: VTU uses the formula: Percentage = (CGPA - 0.75) × 10
faq2: For campus placements, VTU students usually need above 6.75 CGPA (60%).

name: Anna University
desc: Anna University CGPA to percentage converter for engineering students in Tamil Nadu.
faq1: Anna University uses absolute grading. The formula is: Percentage = CGPA × 10
faq2: A CGPA of 8.0 equals exactly 80%.

name: AKTU (UPTU)
desc: Check your AKTU B.Tech CGPA to percentage conversion online.
faq1: AKTU (formerly UPTU) uses: Percentage = (CGPA - 0.75) × 10
faq2: AKTU follows a strict grading system for engineering where 6.75 CGPA is First Class.

name: KTU (Kerala)
desc: Kerala Technological University (KTU) CGPA to percentage calculator.
faq1: KTU uses the formula: Percentage = (CGPA × 10) - 3.75
faq2: A CGPA of 7.0 in KTU equals 66.25%.

name: Pune University (SPPU)
desc: Pune University (Savitribai Phule Pune University) CGPA to percentage calculator.
faq1: For CGPA >= 6.0, SPPU uses Percentage = (CGPA - 0.75) × 10. Otherwise, it uses CGPA × 8.8.
faq2: SPPU's formula has variations depending on the pattern (2015 vs 2019).

name: Delhi University
desc: Delhi University (DU) CGPA to percentage conversion.
faq1: DU officially uses the formula: Percentage = CGPA × 9.5
faq2: To get above 90%, you need a DU CGPA of at least 9.48.

name: CBSE Board
desc: CBSE Class 10th and 12th CGPA to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: CBSE uses the standard formula: Percentage = CGPA × 9.5
faq2: To score 95%, you need a perfect 10 CGPA.

name: JNTU Hyderabad (JNTUH)
desc: JNTU Hyderabad (JNTUH) B.Tech CGPA to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: JNTUH uses the formula: Percentage = (CGPA - 0.5) × 10
faq2: A CGPA of 6.5 in JNTUH corresponds to 60% (First Class).

name: Gujarat Tech University (GTU)
desc: GTU SPI / CPI / CGPA to Percentage Calculator for Diploma & BE.
faq1: GTU uses the official formula: Percentage = (SPI / CPI / CGPA - 0.5) × 10
faq2: To get First Class with Distinction, GTU requires a CPI of 7.5 or higher.

name: Calicut University
desc: Calicut University (UOC) Grade Point Average to Percentage Converter.
faq1: Calicut University (UOC) uses the 10-point scale: Percentage = CGPA × 10
faq2: First Class in Calicut University is awarded at 6.0 CGPA (60%).

name: JNTU Kakinada (JNTUK)
desc: JNTU Kakinada (JNTUK) R19 / R20 B.Tech CGPA to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: JNTUK R19/R20 regulations use: Percentage = (CGPA - 0.75) × 10
faq2: A CGPA of 6.75 in JNTUK corresponds to First Class (60%).

name: Osmania University (OU)
desc: Osmania University (OU) CGPA to Percentage Converter for Degree & Engineering.
faq1: Osmania University uses the official formula: Percentage = (CGPA - 0.5) × 10
faq2: A CGPA of 7.0 is equivalent to 65% in Osmania University.

name: RGPV Bhopal
desc: Rajiv Gandhi Proudyogiki Vishwavidyalaya (RGPV) CGPA to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: RGPV B.Tech uses the formula: Percentage = CGPA × 10
faq2: First Division with Honours in RGPV requires a CGPA of 7.5 or higher.

name: BPUT Odisha
desc: Biju Patnaik University of Technology (BPUT) CGPA to Percentage Converter.
faq1: BPUT Odisha uses: Percentage = (CGPA - 0.5) × 10
faq2: A BPUT CGPA of 6.5 equals 60% (First Class).

name: SRM Institute of Tech (SRMIST)
desc: SRM University (SRMIST) CGPA to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: SRMIST uses standard 10-point scaling: Percentage = CGPA × 10
faq2: A CGPA of 9.0+ qualifies for First Class with Distinction at SRM.

name: UP Board (UPMSP)
desc: UP Board High School (10th) & Intermediate (12th) Marks to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: UP Board calculates percentage by dividing total obtained marks by total maximum marks (600 for 10th, 500 for 12th) and multiplying by 100.
faq2: First Division in UP Board is awarded for scoring 60% or higher.

name: Bihar Board (BSEB)
desc: BSEB Bihar Board 10th Matric & 12th Inter Marks to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: Bihar Board percentage formula: (Total Obtained Marks ÷ 500) × 100.
faq2: First Division in BSEB is awarded for scoring 300 marks or more out of 500 (60%).

name: MP Board (MPBSE)
desc: MP Board Class 10th & 12th Marks & Grade Point Percentage Calculator.
faq1: MP Board percentage is calculated as: (Total Obtained Marks ÷ Total Maximum Marks) × 100.
faq2: Passing marks for MP Board theory exams are 33% per subject.

name: Rajasthan Board (RBSE)
desc: RBSE Board 10th & 12th Marks to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: RBSE calculates percentage as: (Obtained Marks ÷ Total Maximum Marks) × 100.
faq2: First Division in RBSE is awarded for scoring 60% or higher.

name: West Bengal Board (WBCHSE / WBBSE)
desc: WBBSE Madhyamik & WBCHSE Higher Secondary Percentage Calculator.
faq1: West Bengal Board percentage formula: (Total Marks Obtained ÷ Total Max Marks) × 100.
faq2: First Division in WB Board is awarded for scoring 60% or above.

name: Karnataka SSLC & PUC Board
desc: Karnataka KSEAB SSLC (10th) & 2nd PUC (12th) Marks to Percentage Calculator.
faq1: Karnataka SSLC percentage formula: (Obtained Marks ÷ 625) × 100. 2nd PUC uses (Obtained Marks ÷ 600) × 100.
faq2: Distinction in Karnataka Board is awarded for 85% or higher.

name: CBSE 10th Result Percentage Calculator 2026
desc: Calculate your CBSE Class 10th result percentage from best of 5 subjects or total CGPA.
faq1: CBSE Class 10 percentage formula: Add marks of top 5 subjects, divide by 5.
faq2: If grades are given in CGPA, multiply CGPA by 9.5 to get your exact percentage.

name: CBSE 12th Result Percentage Calculator 2026
desc: Calculate your CBSE Class 12th result percentage for Science, Commerce, and Arts streams.
faq1: CBSE Class 12 percentage formula: (Total marks in best 5 main subjects ÷ 500) × 100.
faq2: Aggregates for university admission (like DU CUET) usually require top 4 or top 3 subject combinations.
